extracted.intended_audience: educators, workshop presenters, and grant applicants preparing VOTE (vocational-occupational-technical education) curriculum development proposals and state monitors/reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklists for running proposal-writing workshops and for preparing/evaluating vocational-technical curriculum grant proposals (VOTE). Includes stepwise workshop process, editing exercises, component-specific checklists (goals, objectives, evaluation, activities), and the Federal Register review criteria with weights and detailed yes/no items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop process for developing proposal components (seven steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: A seven-step repeated procedure for each project proposal component (goals, objectives, evaluation, activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STEP 1: Presentation describing, explaining, demonstrating the component; participants may ask questions and request examples. STEP 2: Participants develop draft versions using the procedures and criteria from the presentation. STEP 3: Participants self-evaluate drafts using a specially designed checklist, answering each question YES or NO and providing evidence. STEP 4: Participants revise drafts based on self-evaluation. STEP 5: Participants present the revision to the appropriate state monitor for objective third-party evaluation using the same checklist. STEP 6: Participants rework the component in light of the monitor's suggestions. STEP 7: Participants resubmit the end product for approval by the state monitor. (These steps are repeated for each component in order: goals, objectives, evaluation, activities.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision/editing: Short, simple, smooth text
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for revising rough drafts into short, simple, and smooth reading texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directions: Revise the rough draft to remove unnecessary repetitions, non-essential words, and ambiguous references. Revise, compare with a sample revision, then revise again in light of the sample. Emphasizes clarity, brevity, and elimination of ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionnaire drafting: clarity and simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for turning curriculum criteria into a usable questionnaire for curriculum developers/evaluators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a rough draft of curriculum criteria based on Federal Register guidelines; then revise the draft into a questionnaire. Remove complicated questions, ambiguous words, unnecessary repetitions, and non-essential words. Compare with sample 'VOCATIONAL EDUCATION CURRICULUM CRITERIA' and revise again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing Project Goal(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist to determine whether the project goal is properly framed and appropriate for the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer YES/NO and provide evidence. Items include: Is the project goal consistent with Division priorities? Does it address problems described in the statement of needs? Does it treat distinct points separately? Does the goal avoid rationale/explanations/background (i.e., be a concise goal)? Does it avoid specifics that belong in objectives and activities? Does the goal describe the population to be ultimately affected and is that population legitimately served with special project funds? Does the goal describe the general behavior to be affected and the general means to be used? Does the description of means make clear which processes will be used (research, needs assessment, development, adaptation, field-testing, dissemination)?

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing Project Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist to evaluate objectives for clarity, measurability, focus, sequencing, and linkage to goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer YES/NO and provide evidence. Items include: Does each goal have appropriate corresponding objectives? Do objectives lead toward attainment of the goal? Do objectives describe major outcomes and deal with only one major outcome each? Are objectives outcomes-focused rather than procedural details? Do objectives describe specific standards for outcomes and specify deadlines? For objectives leading to behavioral change, do they describe who will be affected, what behavior, and to what degree? Are objectives arranged in an appropriate order? Do objectives provide an adequate basis for selecting appropriate activities and evaluation measures?

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing Project Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist to ensure that evaluation items correspond to objectives and are adequate to determine attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer YES/NO and provide evidence. Items include: Does each objective have appropriate corresponding evaluation items? Do evaluation items likely measure attainment of the corresponding objective? Do evaluation procedures describe what data is to be collected and how? Does the evaluation for each objective specify criteria and realistic/appropriate performance levels? Is the data to be collected adequate? Does the evaluation describe how data will be analyzed? Are data analysis design components present when appropriate (experimental group, control group, pretest, posttest)? Does the plan of data analysis appear valid? Is provision made for formative evaluations to guide project management decisions?

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing Project Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist to judge whether listed activities will lead to objectives, are realistic, assigned, and cost-effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer YES/NO and provide evidence. Items include: Does each objective have appropriate corresponding activities? Do activities seem likely to lead to attainment of objectives? Are activities dated and in chronological order? Are activities visually depicted (timeline/flowchart) to be easy to follow? Are timeframes realistic? Do activities indicate who is responsible and do those persons have necessary expertise? Are unnecessary, duplicative, overly expensive, too time-consuming, wasteful or otherwise undesirable activities eliminated? Do activities provide for data collection and analysis? Do activities include preparing required reports (quarterly progress, final report, final claim)?

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Review Criterion: Need and Problems (score 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register criterion evaluating clarity and appropriateness of need within the specified consortium of states and responsiveness to problems (20 points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application should clearly define the need for the project and the need within the specified consortium. It should indicate responsiveness to problems rather than symptoms. Detailed yes/no checklist items provided include: Has a systematic method of ferreting out key symptoms been identified? Has a logical analysis been applied to information on symptoms? Has documentation been provided explaining how problems were identified? Have problems been translated into recognized needs? Have institutional, administrative, teacher, student/parent, and concerned community group needs been recognized? Has an adequate and realistic/meaningful response been made to the needs, including addressing needs at all levels (institutional, administrative, teacher, student/parents, community groups)? (Refer to checklist items 101–164.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Review Criterion: Objectives (score 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal criterion assessing clarity, attainability, and measurability of objectives (10 points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should be clearly stated, capable of being attained by the proposed procedures, and capable of being measured. Checklist asks: Have the objectives been stated clearly? Are they capable of being attained and by the proposed procedures? Are they capable of being measured and measured by the proposed evaluation design? (Checklist items 201–222.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Review Criterion: Plan (score 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal criterion evaluating the management plan, functions, services, and procedures to accomplish them (20 points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The management plan should show the functions to be performed and services to be provided, and the procedures for accomplishing each should be delineated. Checklist questions include: Does the management plan show functions to be performed? Does it show services to be provided? Does it delineate procedures for accomplishing each function and each service? (Checklist items 301–322.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Review Criterion: Results (score 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal criterion assessing identification and description of proposed outcomes in terms of potential impact and program purposes (20 points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed outcomes should be identified and described in terms of potential impact at national, state, and local levels, in terms of the overall program purposes, and in terms of cost-effectiveness and efficiency. Checklist items ask whether the proposal identifies and describes outcomes, potential impacts at national/state/local levels, link to overall program purposes, and outcomes in terms of cost-effectiveness and efficiency. (Checklist items 401–441.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Review Criterion: Institutional Capability (score 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal criterion evaluating the applicant's current curriculum strengths and ability to initiate and maintain liaison functions with consortium states (15 points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application should clearly set forth current curriculum strengths and the capability to immediately initiate and maintain liaison functions with consortium states; past track record in maintaining liaison functions should be described. Checklist items include documentation of strengths, capability, and past performance. (Checklist items 501–521.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Review Criterion: Personnel (score 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal criterion assessing qualifications, experience, responsibilities, and time commitment of key staff (10 points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifications and experience backgrounds of key staff should be appropriate to the project requirements; specific responsibilities should be identified for each key staff; at least one key staff person should devote a minimum of 50% of his/her time to the project. Checklist items 601–631 capture these points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Review Criterion: Budget/Cost (score 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal criterion evaluating whether estimated cost is provided and reasonable in relation to anticipated results, geographic area, scope, and duration (5 points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items include: Has an estimated cost been provided? Is the estimated cost reasonable overall? Is it reasonable in relation to anticipated results, the geographic area, the scope of the project, and the duration of the project? (Checklist items 701–715.)
